confidence_notes: I used web searches for the food and drink anchors. Wise, Numbeo (Nov 2026), Moneyfarm and uHomes broadly agree: cappuccino about GBP 4.1-4.3, a domestic draught pint about GBP 6.5-7.0, an inexpensive meal about GBP 20, and a mid-range three-course meal for two about GBP 80 without drinks. These are high-confidence. I converted to USD with an assumed GBP/USD rate of about 1.34. I did not search for this rate, so a different rate would shift all anchors proportionally. The pricing window is July 2026, but the search results are from Nov 2026, so the July figures could be slightly different. No aggregated 2026 London figure was found for wine. That estimate (about GBP 8.5 for a 175ml restaurant glass) comes from the ONS UK national average (GBP 5.17 in Jan 2025), a London premium of about 24% over the UK for pub drinks, and a 2026 report of house wine up to GBP 7.95. No search result gave a cocktail price. The cocktail estimate (about GBP 14) comes from my general knowledge and the local relationship to beer (about 2x the pint price), so its confidence is lower. The four accommodation anchors are my own estimates for peak July demand in central London, without searches. They are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: I based the food and drink anchors directly on aggregated London cost-of-living data, not a comparable city. Where London-specific drink data were thin, I used UK national averages adjusted by London's observed pub-price premium. For the accommodation estimates, I treated London in July as a high-cost peak-season Western European capital, similar to Paris or Amsterdam in summer.
